nodes.label: code-reviewer agent
nodes.rationale: Reviews the diff against CLAUDE.md before Claude pushes (ADR-0013); reports findings only and never edits files, so review stays independent of implementation.

nodes.label: Push safety check (no rewritten remote commits)
nodes.norm_label: push safety check (no rewritten remote commits)
nodes.rationale: Only TRK/TREK branches or ui-evidence; git merge-base --is-ancestor Trekky/<branch> HEAD must succeed so no remote commit was amended or rebased.

nodes.label: Ordered review checklist
nodes.rationale: Correctness, tenancy/security, module boundaries, activity log, API contract, tests, scope, conventions, buildability, push safety; ranked findings split into must-fix and suggestions.

nodes.label: Second-org cross-tenant test rule
nodes.rationale: Any test touching tenant data adds a second org and asserts it cannot see the first org's data.

nodes.label: Deterministic tests (TimeProvider, no sleeps)
nodes.rationale: Behaviour-named tests, one behaviour per test, no real clock or order dependence; never report tests as passing unless seen to pass.

nodes.label: test-writer agent
nodes.rationale: Writes xUnit unit tests for domain rules, WebApplicationFactory integration tests per endpoint, Vitest + Testing Library component tests and Playwright e2e for key flows.

nodes.label: /adr skill
nodes.rationale: Writes docs/adr/NNNN-<kebab-title>.md from 0000-template.md with Status Proposed, Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives; reuses Notion agreements instead of re-deciding.

nodes.label: <Name>DbContext with Schema constant and migrations in Persistence
nodes.norm_label: <name>dbcontext with schema constant and migrations in persistence

nodes.label: Five module layer projects (Api, Application, Domain, Infrastructure, Persistence)
nodes.norm_label: five module layer projects (api, application, domain, infrastructure, persistence)
nodes.rationale: Only <Name>Module and Application/Contracts are public, everything else internal sealed; Domain has no EF Core or ASP.NET Core.

nodes.label: ModuleLayeringTests
nodes.rationale: Project references are transitive, so only this test stops Api from using the DbContext.

nodes.label: Squash merge pinned with --match-head-commit
nodes.rationale: Merge exactly the reviewed commit; never --admin; check Trekky/dev before retrying after a GitHub error.

nodes.label: TRK workflow (pick, branch, implement, verify/review, commit, push, merge, promote)
nodes.norm_label: trk workflow (pick, branch, implement, verify/review, commit, push, merge, promote)
nodes.rationale: Branch from Trekky/dev (local dev falls behind because merges happen on GitHub); the committed tree must be the one that passed verify and review.

nodes.label: NU190x vulnerable package rule
nodes.rationale: Bump to a patched version in Directory.Packages.props; never suppress the audit.

nodes.label: /verify skill
nodes.rationale: Backend restore/build/test, frontend lint/test/build, then runtime smoke; report a pass/fail/not-run table and only call a change verified when every step passed.

nodes.label: Activity log via outbox (ADR-0011)
nodes.rationale: Every state change writes an activity_event in the same transaction; the stream later feeds notifications, real-time, webhooks and AI context.

nodes.label: API conventions (/api/v1, RFC 9457, cursor pagination, ETag/If-Match, TypedResults)
nodes.norm_label: api conventions (/api/v1, rfc 9457, cursor pagination, etag/if-match, typedresults)

nodes.label: Auth: ASP.NET Core Identity + OpenIddict in-app
nodes.norm_label: auth: asp.net core identity + openiddict in-app

nodes.label: Branches and promotion dev -> staging -> main (ADR-0022)
nodes.norm_label: branches and promotion dev -> staging -> main (adr-0022)
nodes.rationale: Protected branches with four CI checks; admins are not blocked by GitHub, so the rules are self-enforced.

nodes.label: Buildable history
nodes.rationale: Every TRK verified locally before push; combine TRKs into one commit if one alone would not build or run.

nodes.label: Davit gives requirements; Claude does the rest (ADR-0023)
nodes.norm_label: davit gives requirements; claude does the rest (adr-0023)
nodes.rationale: Claude verifies, reviews, merges, promotes, deploys and tags; asks Davit only for requirements, product decisions, money, credentials and destructive prod operations.

nodes.label: Modular monolith (IModule, schema per module)
nodes.rationale: Modules talk through public contracts or events, never another module's internals or cross-schema joins.

nodes.label: One TRK at a time, in order
nodes.norm_label: one trk at a time, in order

nodes.label: Postman collection updated with endpoint changes (ADR-0008)
nodes.norm_label: postman collection updated with endpoint changes (adr-0008)

nodes.label: Scope versions (v0.1 Skeleton to v1.1 Hosting and desktop app)
nodes.norm_label: scope versions (v0.1 skeleton to v1.1 hosting and desktop app)

nodes.label: Storage (S3 API, ADR-0006) and SMTP mail
nodes.norm_label: storage (s3 api, adr-0006) and smtp mail

nodes.label: Tenancy via org_id + Postgres RLS
nodes.rationale: Never rely on WHERE org_id alone; app.org_id per connection; API connects as trekky_app, migrations as trekky_owner; EnableTenantRowLevelSecurity never hand-written.

nodes.label: TrekkyPolicies roles per endpoint (ADR-0026)
nodes.rationale: ReadWork, EditWork, ManageProjects, ManageMembers; EndpointPolicyTests fails otherwise; UI hides via usePermissions but the API is the guard.

nodes.label: Trekky (lean task tracker)
nodes.rationale: Later products (Trekky Docs, context layer, AI agent) build on it, so every entity is machine-readable from day one: stable keys, structured fields, full history.

nodes.label: UUIDv7 internal IDs, human keys external
nodes.norm_label: uuidv7 internal ids, human keys external

nodes.label: Single work_item table (type + parent_id + custom JSONB)
nodes.norm_label: single work_item table (type + parent_id + custom jsonb)

nodes.label: Nightly pg_dump backup service
nodes.rationale: Dump as Postgres superuser because tables force RLS so only a superuser sees every tenant; 14 days kept; optional offsite copy via rclone S3.

nodes.label: Caddy web service (static app + same-origin proxy)
nodes.norm_label: caddy web service (static app + same-origin proxy)

nodes.label: Deploy a new version procedure
nodes.rationale: List new migrations, take a fresh backup, note HEAD for rollback, checkout detached Trekky/main, up, check migrate exit 0 and health; stop for Davit if a migration drops/renames/rewrites data.

nodes.label: migrate service (EF Core migrations as trekky_owner)
nodes.norm_label: migrate service (ef core migrations as trekky_owner)

nodes.label: Production Compose stack on home host (ADR-0015)
nodes.norm_label: production compose stack on home host (adr-0015)
nodes.rationale: All durable state outside containers (volumes, secrets, backups, .env) so the same images can move to Azure Container Apps + Neon (TRK-29).

nodes.label: Tailscale Funnel public HTTPS
nodes.rationale: No router ports or domain needed; auth key not ephemeral and not tagged; disable key expiry so the public address keeps working.

nodes.label: Refresh token in Windows Credential Manager
nodes.norm_label: refresh token in windows credential manager

nodes.label: Desktop sign-in via system browser and trekky:// callback (ADR-0019)
nodes.norm_label: desktop sign-in via system browser and trekky:// callback (adr-0019)

nodes.label: MSI installer (fixed WiX upgrade code, unsigned)
nodes.norm_label: msi installer (fixed wix upgrade code, unsigned)

nodes.label: Trekky for Windows Tauri 2 shell (ADR-0018)
nodes.rationale: Shell only keeps server address, single instance and navigation; every screen is React.

nodes.label: Desktop release by desktop-v tag (ADR-0020)
nodes.rationale: Draft release with signed MSI and latest.json, checked by install, then published as latest; other releases must use --latest=false or installed apps lose the update feed.

nodes.label: Pinned Rust toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml)
nodes.rationale: Stops new stable clippy lints from failing unrelated PRs.

nodes.label: Updater minisign key (ADR-0024)
nodes.rationale: Installed apps trust only the built-in public key; a lost key means manual reinstall, a leaked key needs a transition release signed with the old key.

nodes.label: Trekky App Icon 128x128@2x (white T on blue rounded square)
nodes.norm_label: trekky app icon 128x128@2x (white t on blue rounded square)

nodes.label: Trekky Desktop App Icon (128x128)
nodes.rationale: A white bold letter 'T' centred on a rounded-square bright blue background; the 'T' monogram stands for Trekky and serves as the Windows desktop (Tauri 2) app icon.

nodes.label: Trekky Desktop App Icon (32x32)
nodes.rationale: Small app icon for the Trekky for Windows Tauri 2 desktop shell: a white bold letter T on a blue rounded square, the Trekky brand mark at 32x32 for taskbar and window use.

nodes.label: Trekky Desktop App Icon
nodes.rationale: 512x512 app icon: a bold white rounded-stroke capital letter T centred on a solid bright blue (#2563EB-like) rounded-square tile. The T stands for Trekky; the flat two-colour design keeps the mark legible at small Windows taskbar and installer sizes.

nodes.label: ADR Template
nodes.rationale: Fixed shape for every ADR: Status (Proposed | Agreed | Rejected | Superseded), Date, Deciders, Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered.

nodes.label: .NET 10 Modular Monolith
nodes.rationale: One engineer, ~1 hour a week, no paid services: one process, one deploy, one database keeps ops near zero and self-hosting simple; module boundaries make a later split a refactor, not a rewrite. Microservices rejected for network/deploy/observability cost; layered monolith rejected because it would tangle Docs and the agent into one model.

nodes.label: IModule Contract (schema + DbContext per module)
nodes.rationale: Each module owns its Postgres schema and DbContext, implements IModule and talks to others only through public contracts or events; internals stay internal.

nodes.label: Non-.NET Service Admission Rule
nodes.rationale: A non-.NET service is allowed only if: no reasonable .NET option exists, it sits behind a narrow HTTP/queue contract owning no data others read, and its extra build/deploy/monitoring cost is accepted in an ADR.

nodes.label: ADR-0002: Multi-tenancy - shared database, org_id + Postgres RLS
nodes.norm_label: adr-0002: multi-tenancy - shared database, org_id + postgres rls

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Tenancy (no tenant = no rows)
nodes.rationale: current_setting(..., true) returns NULL without a tenant, so queries see nothing and cannot write.

nodes.label: Postgres Row-Level Security on org_id
nodes.rationale: Tenant data must be invisible to other orgs even under bugs in our own queries; one isolation mechanism for every module, and a forgotten filter returns nothing. DB-per-tenant is overkill, schema-per-tenant conflicts with schema-per-module, and EF global filters alone leak on one missed filter or raw SQL.

nodes.label: EF Core Tenant Connection Interceptor
nodes.rationale: Runs set_config('app.org_id', ...) on connection open using the org_id claim; Npgsql resets session state on pool return so the tenant cannot leak.

nodes.label: ADR-0003: Authentication - ASP.NET Core Identity + OpenIddict in-app
nodes.norm_label: adr-0003: authentication - asp.net core identity + openiddict in-app
nodes.rationale: No extra service to run (Authentik/Keycloak dropped), no paid IdP that blocks self-hosting, and bearer tokens needed anyway for the MCP server and agent, so cookie-only BFF rejected.

nodes.label: Authorization Code + PKCE Web Flow
nodes.rationale: Resource-owner password grant is removed in OAuth 2.1; the login page sets an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, then /connect/authorize and /connect/token issue tokens.

nodes.label: JWT Access Tokens + Rotating Refresh Tokens
nodes.norm_label: jwt access tokens + rotating refresh tokens
nodes.rationale: 15-minute RS256 access tokens; refresh tokens rotate on every use and reuse of an old one revokes the chain; tokens kept in memory only, silent prompt=none re-auth after reload.

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/auth/sign-up
nodes.rationale: Creates user, organization and Owner membership in one transaction.

nodes.label: ADR-0004: POC hosting - Oracle Always Free VM with Docker Compose (Deferred)
nodes.norm_label: adr-0004: poc hosting - oracle always free vm with docker compose (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Deferred 2026-10-30 because the Oracle VM could not be created; to be superseded by ADR-0015. Production stack kept on branch TRK-9-oracle-vm-deploy (PR #11).

nodes.label: Oracle Cloud Always Free ARM64 VM
nodes.norm_label: oracle cloud always free arm64 vm
nodes.rationale: Zero hosting cost and the same Compose stack as local and self-hosted; risk of idle reclamation mitigated by off-VM backups and a restore drill.

nodes.label: ADR-0005: Identifiers - UUIDv7 internally, human keys externally
nodes.norm_label: adr-0005: identifiers - uuidv7 internally, human keys externally

nodes.label: work_items.item_counters Counter Row
nodes.rationale: UPDATE ... RETURNING in the inserting transaction gives gapless, concurrency-safe numbers; sequences per project rejected because they are not transactional.

nodes.label: UUIDv7 Primary Keys (Guid.CreateVersion7)
nodes.rationale: Time-ordered inserts keep B-trees sequential; IDs exist before save (helps outbox events and tests). Bigint leaks volume, UUIDv4 fragments indexes, Postgres uuidv7() needs PG18.

nodes.label: Work Item Key (PROJECT-n)
nodes.rationale: Keys are for display and lookup; relationships always use UUIDs. The item stores its own copy of the project key so it never reads the projects module.

nodes.label: ADR-0006: Object storage - remove MinIO, code against S3 API
nodes.norm_label: adr-0006: object storage - remove minio, code against s3 api

nodes.label: MinIO Removal
nodes.rationale: MinIO community edition ended; images deleted from Docker Hub so docker compose up failed; last build gets no security fixes; nothing stores files yet.

nodes.label: Code Only Against the S3 API
nodes.norm_label: code only against the s3 api
nodes.rationale: AWS SDK for .NET with configurable endpoint makes the storage server a deployment choice, not a code dependency.

nodes.label: SeaweedFS (proposed S3 replacement)
nodes.rationale: Proposed for local dev and self-hosting; Garage (AGPL), RustFS (young), Ceph (too heavy), MinIO AIStor (licence/telemetry) and Postgres blobs considered.

nodes.label: ADR-0007: Reading a user's own memberships before a tenant is known
nodes.norm_label: adr-0007: reading a user's own memberships before a tenant is known

nodes.label: user_self_read SELECT-only RLS Policy
nodes.rationale: Login and refresh must find the user's org before a token exists; BYPASSRLS role too broad, SECURITY DEFINER blocked by FORCE RLS, org_id on user row breaks with multiple orgs. Kept narrow: SELECT only, transaction-local, one table.

nodes.label: ADR-0008: Keep a Postman collection in the repo
nodes.norm_label: adr-0008: keep a postman collection in the repo

nodes.label: postman/Trekky.postman_collection.json
nodes.rationale: Manual testing must start fast; Postman's OAuth helper cannot reach the session cookie, so scripts run the code+PKCE flow and store tokens as collection variables. Updated in the same commit as any endpoint change, one folder per module, no secrets.

nodes.label: Five Layer Projects (Api, Application, Domain, Infrastructure, Persistence)
nodes.norm_label: five layer projects (api, application, domain, infrastructure, persistence)
nodes.rationale: Davit's PR #7 review asked that dependency direction be checked, not just agreed; one project with folders let endpoints use the DbContext and put validation in Domain. Four- and three-project splits rejected for mixing concerns.

nodes.label: Identity Domain Exception (User : IdentityUser<Guid>)
nodes.rationale: Putting User in Infrastructure would create a cycle (Persistence DbContext needs User, Infrastructure needs DbContext), so Identity Domain references Microsoft.Extensions.Identity.Stores.

nodes.label: ADR-0010: Frontend stack and token handling in the web app
nodes.norm_label: adr-0010: frontend stack and token handling in the web app

nodes.label: AuthSession (in-memory tokens per tab)
nodes.rationale: Adds bearer token, refreshes before expiry and after 401, one refresh at a time because refresh tokens are single-use; no tokens in localStorage.

nodes.label: React Router + TanStack Query + Tailwind v4/shadcn-ui + Vitest/Playwright
nodes.norm_label: react router + tanstack query + tailwind v4/shadcn-ui + vitest/playwright
nodes.rationale: TanStack Query covers server state so no Redux/Zustand; shadcn copies plain accessible components into the repo instead of heavy MUI/Chakra.

nodes.label: openapi-fetch Client (src/api/schema.d.ts)
nodes.rationale: Types plus a thin client; hand-written types drift, full generators produce too much code. schema.d.ts must be regenerated and committed on endpoint changes.

nodes.label: Same-Origin Hosting Requirement (web, /api, /connect)
nodes.rationale: The SameSite=Strict session cookie must reach /connect/authorize, so production must serve all three behind one origin; SameSite is the only CSRF defence for logout.

nodes.label: ADR-0011: Outbox dispatcher reads pending events across tenants via scoped RLS policy
nodes.norm_label: adr-0011: outbox dispatcher reads pending events across tenants via scoped rls policy

nodes.label: outbox_dispatch Read-Only RLS Policy
nodes.rationale: Dispatcher has no tenant but must see every org's pending rows. BYPASSRLS role far too broad; dispatch-after-commit leaves crashed events waiting forever; direct writes would cross module schemas; SECURITY DEFINER still needs BYPASSRLS. Narrow: read-only, unprocessed rows, outbox tables only, transaction-local.

nodes.label: OutboxDispatcher
nodes.rationale: Single dispatcher, at-least-once delivery, no FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (would need cross-tenant UPDATE); add a lease or advisory lock with multiple instances.

nodes.label: ADR-0012: UI test screenshots on a ui-evidence branch
nodes.norm_label: adr-0012: ui test screenshots on a ui-evidence branch

nodes.label: ui-evidence Orphan Branch
nodes.rationale: GitHub has no API to attach images to comments and gists reject binaries, while test runs must end clean locally; an orphan evidence-only branch, never merged, pushed fast-forward via a temporary worktree. Layout TRK-<n>/<date>/<nn>-<what>.png with report.md; synthetic data only since the repo is public.

nodes.label: ADR-0013: Claude verifies, reviews and pushes TRK branches
nodes.norm_label: adr-0013: claude verifies, reviews and pushes trk branches
nodes.rationale: Davit's hour went into running builds and pushing instead of reviewing; Claude already runs /verify and code-reviewer. Partly superseded by ADR-0023 (merging, promoting, deploying).

nodes.label: Push Only When Green Rule
nodes.rationale: /verify and code-reviewer both pass on the exact tree being committed, re-run after every fix; if something cannot run, do not push. Only TRK branches and ui-evidence; no history rewrites.

nodes.label: ADR-0014: Keep every revision of a work item in a Postgres table
nodes.norm_label: adr-0014: keep every revision of a work item in a postgres table

nodes.label: work_items.current_revision counter under ItemLocks row lock
nodes.norm_label: work_items.current_revision counter under itemlocks row lock
nodes.rationale: Incremented in the same UPDATE under the edit row lock so two edits never get the same revision number; no-op edits and rank moves write nothing.

nodes.label: work_items.work_item_revisions (append-only JSONB snapshots)
nodes.rationale: Activity events record what changed, not what the item was; description edits lose old text. Full snapshots in the existing Postgres keep one database, one backup, one transaction and RLS; rejected events-replay, snapshot-in-event, triggers, temporal extensions, separate NoSQL store and event sourcing.

nodes.label: ADR-0015: Home machine behind Tailscale Funnel; Azure Container Apps + Neon later
nodes.norm_label: adr-0015: home machine behind tailscale funnel; azure container apps + neon later

nodes.label: Azure Container Apps + Neon Postgres move (TRK-29)
nodes.norm_label: azure container apps + neon postgres move (trk-29)
nodes.rationale: Neon direct (unpooled) connection is required because TenantConnectionInterceptor sets app.org_id per session, which a transaction-mode pooler does not keep; Data Protection keys need PersistKeysTo with SetApplicationName.

nodes.label: Home host Compose stack behind Tailscale Funnel
nodes.norm_label: home host compose stack behind tailscale funnel
nodes.rationale: Oracle free VM could not be created; Funnel is free, needs no open ports, domain or certificate management. Every part built to move unchanged to Azure: settings from env vars, keys outside containers, nothing on container disk.

nodes.label: Nightly pg_dump backup kept 14 days (optional rclone off-machine copy)
nodes.norm_label: nightly pg_dump backup kept 14 days (optional rclone off-machine copy)

nodes.label: ADR-0016: Trekky tracks itself in project TREK; Notion TRK keys stay as history
nodes.norm_label: adr-0016: trekky tracks itself in project trek; notion trk keys stay as history

nodes.label: TREK project key for branches and commits after the switch
nodes.norm_label: trek project key for branches and commits after the switch
nodes.rationale: Trekky numbers items itself from 1, so importing into TRK would give TRK-1..~40 a second meaning; a new key keeps one meaning per key and old commits readable. Imported titles start with the Notion TRK key.

nodes.label: ADR-0017: Desktop app signs in as its own OAuth client; CORS origins from configuration
nodes.norm_label: adr-0017: desktop app signs in as its own oauth client; cors origins from configuration

nodes.label: Cors:AllowedOrigins (bearer only, no credentials)
nodes.rationale: No origin allowed by default; Development and home host allow http://tauri.localhost; credentials never allowed so the session cookie is never sent cross-origin; origins are configuration so the Azure move changes no code.

nodes.label: trekky://auth/callback custom-scheme redirect
nodes.rationale: Chosen over RFC 8252 loopback redirect because Tauri's deep-link plugin makes it simpler and needs no local HTTP listener; PKCE makes intercepted codes useless.

nodes.label: trekky-desktop public native OAuth client (PKCE, 90-day rotating refresh tokens)
nodes.norm_label: trekky-desktop public native oauth client (pkce, 90-day rotating refresh tokens)
nodes.rationale: Separate client lets desktop tokens be told apart (client_id) and revoked without touching web sessions; a desktop app shares no cookie with the system browser so it must keep a refresh token. 90 days matches native-app defaults; never-expiring rejected for lost laptops.

nodes.label: ADR-0018: The desktop app is a thin Tauri shell; its screens live in the web app
nodes.norm_label: adr-0018: the desktop app is a thin tauri shell; its screens live in the web app

nodes.label: Fixed WiX upgrade code 6ACA28C5-222C-4774-AA84-12039D71D793 + bundled WebView2 offline installer
nodes.norm_label: fixed wix upgrade code 6aca28c5-222c-4774-aa84-12039d71d793 + bundled webview2 offline installer
nodes.rationale: Every version upgrades the last in place, never change it; offline WebView2 installer avoids failing offline or on Windows 10 machines without WebView2, at about 170 MB cost.

nodes.label: Shell commands: server_settings, set_server_url, open_in_browser, load/save_refresh_token, auth-callback event
nodes.norm_label: shell commands: server_settings, set_server_url, open_in_browser, load/save_refresh_token, auth-callback event

nodes.label: Thin Tauri 2 shell loading the web app from http://tauri.localhost
nodes.norm_label: thin tauri 2 shell loading the web app from http://tauri.localhost
nodes.rationale: Screens written twice (React plus Rust) would double UI, i18n, accessibility and test work; the shell does only what a browser cannot: server address setting, single instance, keep the window on the app. Remote URL rejected because the app could not show its own can't-reach-server screen.

nodes.label: ADR-0019: Desktop sign-in through the system browser; refresh token in Credential Manager
nodes.norm_label: adr-0019: desktop sign-in through the system browser; refresh token in credential manager

nodes.label: Refresh token in Windows Credential Manager (service Trekky, per server origin, Local persistence)
nodes.norm_label: refresh token in windows credential manager (service trekky, per server origin, local persistence)

nodes.label: Interactive /connect/authorize without session redirects to /login?returnTo=
nodes.rationale: returnTo followed only when it starts with /connect/authorize? on the same origin; prompt=none and POST still get login_required so web silent sign-in is unchanged; avoids a second server-rendered login UI.

nodes.label: Reference refresh tokens (OpenIddict UseReferenceRefreshTokens)
nodes.rationale: A self-contained refresh token is about 3.3 KB, over Credential Manager's 2,560-byte limit; a short handle is worthless once revoked. Chunking across entries rejected as fragile.

nodes.label: Desktop sign-in via /connect/authorize in the system browser
nodes.norm_label: desktop sign-in via /connect/authorize in the system browser
nodes.rationale: RFC 8252 advises native apps against embedded login; passwords stay in the browser and an existing browser session is reused. In-app login form would need SameSite=None and credentialed CORS, weakening the web app.

nodes.label: ADR-0020: Desktop MSI built in CI on every PR, released from a desktop-v tag as a draft
nodes.norm_label: adr-0020: desktop msi built in ci on every pr, released from a desktop-v tag as a draft

nodes.label: desktop-v<version> tag creates a draft GitHub release (unsigned MSI)
nodes.norm_label: desktop-v<version> tag creates a draft github release (unsigned msi)
nodes.rationale: Drafts let a release be checked before users see it; the tag must match the version in tauri.conf.json, Cargo.toml and package.json; versions are major.minor.patch only because Windows Installer takes no pre-release labels.

nodes.label: Desktop CI workflow on windows-latest (version check, lint, test, MSI artifact 14 days)
nodes.norm_label: desktop ci workflow on windows-latest (version check, lint, test, msi artifact 14 days)
nodes.rationale: Without CI a PR could break the desktop app unseen; building only on tags would surface breakage at release time. tauri-action rejected as a third-party action with write access.

nodes.label: ADR-0021: Trekky is licensed under AGPL-3.0-only
nodes.norm_label: adr-0021: trekky is licensed under agpl-3.0-only

nodes.label: AGPL-3.0-only licence
nodes.rationale: Lets teams self-host and contribute while section 13 closes the hosting loophole of plain GPL; OSI-approved (as Plane, Cal.com, Grafana). 'Only' keeps control of terms. FSL, BSL, Apache-2.0, MIT rejected.

nodes.label: Dependency licence compatibility check (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, MPL-2.0 crates...)
nodes.norm_label: dependency licence compatibility check (mit, apache-2.0, bsd, mpl-2.0 crates...)

nodes.label: ADR-0022: dev, staging and main are protected on GitHub
nodes.norm_label: adr-0022: dev, staging and main are protected on github

nodes.label: Branch protection: PRs only, four required CI checks, no force-push or deletion, enforce_admins false
nodes.norm_label: branch protection: prs only, four required ci checks, no force-push or deletion, enforce_admins false
nodes.rationale: Repository became public (TRK-22) so free-plan protection is possible; a duplicate merge after a 502 showed how direct actions go wrong. No approving review required because a single maintainer cannot approve his own PR; enforce_admins false keeps Davit's emergency override; strict false keeps stacked PRs mergeable.

nodes.label: Required checks: Backend (build + test), Frontend (lint + test + build), E2E (Playwright), Docker images (build)
nodes.norm_label: required checks: backend (build + test), frontend (lint + test + build), e2e (playwright), docker images (build)

nodes.label: ADR-0023: Davit gives the requirements; Claude does the rest, through to production
nodes.norm_label: adr-0023: davit gives the requirements; claude does the rest, through to production

nodes.label: Deploy main to the home host after promotion (list migrations, fresh backup, deploy, check health)
nodes.norm_label: deploy main to the home host after promotion (list migrations, fresh backup, deploy, check health)

nodes.label: Merge gate: verify + review on exact tree, evidence comment, green checks, --match-head-commit, squash into dev
nodes.norm_label: merge gate: verify + review on exact tree, evidence comment, green checks, --match-head-commit, squash into dev

nodes.label: Davit provides requirements; Claude implements, merges, promotes, deploys, releases
nodes.norm_label: davit provides requirements; claude implements, merges, promotes, deploys, releases
nodes.rationale: Davit has about 1 hour a week and reviewed green PRs waited days for one click; guarantees carry over via /verify, code-reviewer, green CI (ADR-0022) and evidence (ADR-0012). Davit keeps requirements, product decisions, money, credentials and destructive production operations.

nodes.label: ADR-0024: The desktop app updates itself from signed GitHub releases
nodes.norm_label: adr-0024: the desktop app updates itself from signed github releases

nodes.label: Update feed latest.json on GitHub releases/latest
nodes.norm_label: update feed latest.json on github releases/latest
nodes.rationale: Only the newest published release marked latest is read, so drafts reach nobody; other releases must use --latest=false. Hosting on the home server rejected because the feed would move with the server.

nodes.label: Tag-only signing step (TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY secrets)
nodes.rationale: Signing every CI build would expose the key to every npm and cargo build script on PRs; only desktop-v tags sign, in a separate step after the build.

nodes.label: Tauri updater plugin with Trekky's own minisign key pair
nodes.norm_label: tauri updater plugin with trekky's own minisign key pair
nodes.rationale: The MSI is not code-signed, so updates must verify their origin themselves; requireSignedVersion refuses changed MSIs, swapped feeds and replayed old releases. The key cannot be replaced without stranding users, so it is kept offline and in secrets only.

nodes.norm_label: adr-0025: colours come only from theme tokens

nodes.label: Theme tokens in frontend/src/index.css via Tailwind utilities
nodes.norm_label: theme tokens in frontend/src/index.css via tailwind utilities
nodes.rationale: Raw colours ignore the theme, escape contrast checks and must be changed by hand per theme; tokens make a colour change one edit and a new theme one block. Tailwind palette with dark: variants and CSS-in-JS rejected.

nodes.label: ADR-0026: Every endpoint names the role policy for its action
nodes.norm_label: adr-0026: every endpoint names the role policy for its action

nodes.label: EndpointPolicyTests (every endpoint names a policy; role x policy matrix)
nodes.norm_label: endpointpolicytests (every endpoint names a policy; role x policy matrix)

nodes.label: TrekkyPolicies: ReadWork, EditWork, ManageProjects, ManageMembers
nodes.rationale: Invites, members and bot accounts bring other people and the AI into an organization; rules must live in the API, not in which buttons the UI shows. Policies per action, not per role, so moving an action between roles touches one table. Role read from the token's role claim rather than the database per request.

nodes.norm_label: activity event envelope (eventid, eventtype, schemaversion, actor, entity, payload)

nodes.label: Event rules: past tense names, values not IDs, additive within schemaVersion, no rank events
nodes.norm_label: event rules: past tense names, values not ids, additive within schemaversion, no rank events
nodes.rationale: Events feed history, notifications, webhooks and AI context, so they must be stable and self-describing; rank changes would flood history.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox -> dispatcher -> activity.activity_events (at least once)
nodes.norm_label: transactional outbox -> dispatcher -> activity.activity_events (at least once)
nodes.rationale: State change and event commit in one SaveChanges transaction; the dispatcher reads pending rows of every org via the outbox_dispatch policy and sets app.org_id per row; consumers deduplicate on event_id.

nodes.label: rank: fractional index BoardRank (collate C), locked via item_counters
nodes.norm_label: rank: fractional index boardrank (collate c), locked via item_counters
nodes.rationale: A move writes only the moved card's rank; known limit: no rebalancing yet, ~16,000 drops between the same two cards would exceed Postgres's index entry size.

nodes.label: comments table (soft delete, author-only edit, xmin ETag)
nodes.norm_label: comments table (soft delete, author-only edit, xmin etag)

nodes.label: Database roles: trekky_owner (migrations), trekky_app (runtime, no BYPASSRLS)
nodes.norm_label: database roles: trekky_owner (migrations), trekky_app (runtime, no bypassrls)

nodes.label: item_counters (per-project numbering via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT)
nodes.norm_label: item_counters (per-project numbering via insert ... on conflict)
nodes.rationale: Created by the project's first item rather than on ProjectCreated, so an item can be created without waiting for the outbox; the row lock serializes concurrent creates.

nodes.label: memberships table with user_self_read RLS policy
nodes.norm_label: memberships table with user_self_read rls policy
nodes.rationale: Login and token refresh must read the membership before any org_id is known; app.user_id is set transaction-local.

nodes.label: Module schemas: identity, projects, work_items, activity
nodes.norm_label: module schemas: identity, projects, work_items, activity

nodes.label: No foreign keys or joins across module schemas
nodes.norm_label: no foreign keys or joins across module schemas
nodes.rationale: A module stores another module's ID as a plain uuid; consistency is kept by the owning module's API and events.

nodes.label: work_items table (type, status, parent_id, assignee_id, rank, custom, current_revision)
nodes.norm_label: work_items table (type, status, parent_id, assignee_id, rank, custom, current_revision)

nodes.norm_label: optimistic concurrency via postgres xmin exposed as etag

nodes.label: Pre-paint theme script /theme.js (TREK-56)
nodes.rationale: Blocking on purpose to set the theme before first paint; a separate file because the CSP allows no inline scripts.

nodes.label: C2PA Content Credentials Manifest (Claude-provided file)
nodes.rationale: Embedded <metadata><c2pa:manifest> block: a signed provenance record stating Claude provided the file at a user's request and may have created or modified it.

nodes.label: Trekky Favicon (blue rounded square with white T)
nodes.norm_label: trekky favicon (blue rounded square with white t)
nodes.rationale: 32x32 SVG app icon: a rounded square (rx=7) filled with blue #2563eb and a white 'T' monogram drawn as two round-capped 3.5px strokes (top bar x=9..23 at y=10, stem x=16 from y=10..23). The T stands for Trekky and gives the web app (and desktop shell) its brand mark in the browser tab.

nodes.label: AGPL-3.0-only license (ADR-0021)
nodes.rationale: Anyone running a modified Trekky over a network must offer its source; the app's Source code link (frontend/src/lib/sourceCode.ts) points to it.

nodes.label: Web sign-in flow (session cookie + authorization code + PKCE, ADR-0003)
nodes.norm_label: web sign-in flow (session cookie + authorization code + pkce, adr-0003)
nodes.rationale: Tokens stay in memory; reload re-runs the flow with prompt=none from the cookie; access token refreshed before expiry or after 401.

nodes.label: Idempotent forward-only import
nodes.rationale: Items found by Notion key, never created twice, statuses only move forward.

nodes.label: Notion import tool (TRK-21)
nodes.rationale: Moves the Notion task list into project TREK so Trekky tracks itself; Notion key prefixed in the title so old keys stay searchable.
